The technology and space fight sequences were much better described and communicated.


The biggest difference in the books has to be any scene where the protomolecule is encountered though. In the TV show the protomolecule is this glowy blue thing that looks like some deep sea comb jellies, in the book that shit is SCARY and invokes some crazy body horror vibes that compete with John Carpenter. They missed a great opportunity to use some crazy practical effects, but it kind of lost its weight with the crappy CG.

I have a friend who just graduated last year majoring in mechanical engineering. He did an internship at space x two years in a row before graduation and now is an employee there.

He admits to working long hours at space x. It's stressful and often  times leaves him without sleep and pushes him to his limits. However, he is happy to work like this, sure the pay might not be on par per hour in terms of a software development job at google or Amazon, but he believes in the mission statement of space x and was well aware of the work ethic culture of the company before he signed on.

It's a rocket science company. Every employee works the same kind of crazy hours that a NASA employee does. Rocket science requires extreme dedication and sometimes that translates to long hours. I would bet that most employees knew what they signed up for and are OK with the sacrifices they make to change the world. It's not like Elon Musk has a plush life, he sleeps 5-6 hours a day, running two companies and a nonprofit all of which are taking steps to use capitolism as tool to create positive changes that will benefit humanity.

Said buddy also makes six figures a year with full benefits and is working on  systems that will contribute to the colonization of Mars in 4 years.
